result.summary:
Ran scripts/test_parallel.sh (TEST_PARALLEL_N=4, env override, following ISS-0219/anti-patterns.md precedent over this host's raw nproc=16) synchronously via nohup+blocking-poll (never backgrounded via the Bash tool, never Monitor'd, per core-directives.md ISS-0213/ISS-0223). combined: 4626 tests, 6 properties, 38 failures (4594/4632 passed).

Before starting: found a live (not stale) erl.exe (PID 13228, plain `mix test`, fresh sub-second pg_stat_activity queries) in this shared checkout. Confirmed via SendMessage that neither 'main' nor 'gui-review-continuation' owns it -- consistent with docs/anti-patterns.md's documented finding that this host runs multiple untracked concurrent Claude sessions. Did not kill it (no staleness evidence); scripts/test_parallel.sh's own partitioned DBs are isolated from it, so proceeded.

Independently attributed every one of the 38 failures against `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` and each failure's actual stack trace/log output (never against ELIXIR-DEV rework2's reported 39-failure set or count):

18 failures are STRUCTURALLY ATTRIBUTABLE TO THIS BRANCH -- this overturns rework2's classification of 17 of them as 'pre-existing/unrelated':
  - 16x Letflow.Scheduler.PollerTest: lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex (in diff) widened its GenServer state to require a new key (:last_partition_maintenance_run_at) and now unconditionally reads it in handle_info/2's new maybe_run_partition_maintenance/2 call. test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs (NOT in diff, pre-existing, REQ-188/REQ-218/ISS-0421/ISS-0444/ISS-0695 tests) constructs raw partial state maps that don't have the new key -- every one of these 16 crashes with `** (KeyError) key :last_partition_maintenance_run_at not found`, stack trace bottoming in poller.ex:408. Real regression this branch introduced into a test file it never touched.
  - 1x Letflow.Test.TenantTemplateTest ('clone-vs-template parity'): lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex (in diff) registers this branch's 9 new migrations creating partitioned events/events_archive. The actual diff output shows the :clone provisioning path is missing exactly the 7 partition-child tables and 11 PK/FK constraints these migrations create -- Postgres's CREATE TABLE LIKE...INCLUDING ALL cannot replicate PARTITION BY structure or per-partition FKs. This specific failure cannot occur at the merge-base (events/events_archive aren't partitioned there, so there's nothing to be 'missing'), so it is newly introduced by this branch, not pre-existing, even though its root mechanism is an inherent Postgres limitation. rework2 conflated 'inherent DB limitation' with 'pre-existing failure' -- these are different claims here.
  - 1x Letflow.Docs.RequirementStatusInvariantsTest (A9): this branch's own diff to docs/status/requirement_status.v21.yaml appends exactly one history entry (REQ-376 'started') without bumping docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml's declared volume-21 entries count (19 -> should be 20) -- a missed HOW-TO-APPEND step 6.

20 failures are STRUCTURALLY CLEARED AS PRE-EXISTING/ENVIRONMENTAL (route 1: module/dependency absent from git diff; route 3: measured mechanism) -- filed-and-forwarded, not blocking: 4x ApiPipelineIntegrationTest, 4x ServiceCatalogReaperTest, 3x Iss0736OidcLiveRevocationTest, 1x IdentityTest, 3x TenantSchemaReaperTest, 5x AuthPipelineTest. Every one of these has an actual error of either `Postgrex.Error) FATAL 53300 (too_many_connections)` / `DBConnection.ConnectionError` (in test/support/bpm_default_realm_displacement.ex's dedicated-lock acquisition, or plain connection-pool exhaustion), or the by-design ISS-0110/ISS-0414 'another mix test invocation is currently connected' concurrent-invocation guard correctly deferring against the independently-confirmed live PID 13228 session sharing this host's single 100-connection Postgres budget alongside this run's own 4x20=80. None of their modules or test files appear in this branch's diff.

Full per-failure evidence in test/reports/report-20260922-WF02-REQ376-20260922.yaml. Raw logs preserved at /tmp/letflow_test_parallel.7UuFSt (kept automatically by test_parallel.sh on any non-clean exit).
result.next_action: Route back to ELIXIR-DEV for rework: (1) lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex needs to tolerate a state map missing :last_partition_maintenance_run_at (defensive fix) OR test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs's ~16 hand-built state literals need the new field added -- ELIXIR-DEV's call which side per core-directives' 'route real bugs to ELIXIR-DEV rather than loosening the test'; (2) the :clone tenant-provisioning strategy's inability to replicate partitioned events/events_archive (missing 7 tables + 11 constraints) needs either a real fix or an explicit reviewed decision that :clone is out of scope for partitioned tables, with test/support/tenant_template_test.exs updated to match; (3) docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml's volume-21 `entries:` needs bumping from 19 to 20 (trivial, can go with either fix's commit). Do NOT route to RELEASE-VALIDATOR until these are resolved and a clean re-run confirms it.

issues.description: ELIXIR-DEV rework2's full-suite run (step-02a-elixir-dev-rework2.json) misclassified 17 of its 39 failures (16 PollerTest + 1 TenantTemplateTest) as pre-existing/unrelated to REQ-376 without checking git diff --name-only for scheduler.ex/poller.ex/tenant_provisioning.ex, all three of which ARE in this branch's own diff. This step's independent structural re-verification is exactly what caught it -- flagging so future runs on this branch don't re-trust that report's attribution.

This checkout remains shared concurrently with at least one other live, untracked Claude session (PID 13228, plain mix test) for this entire run's duration -- consistent with docs/anti-patterns.md's existing entry from earlier in this same run. Caused 20 of 38 observed failures via Postgres connection contention; none block this step since they're structurally cleared, but a re-run once that session finishes would likely show a cleaner (though not necessarily zero, since the ISS-0110/ISS-0414 guards are concurrency-sensitive by design) failure set for that group.
